meta.purpose: Hand-curated app content for the MVP's five sketch classes. scripts/build_mvp_activity_pack.py joins this with data/evidence_links.json, data/activities.json and data/recommendations.json to produce data/exports/mvp_activity_pack.json.

interaction_types.breath_pacer: Animated in/out pacer with configurable inhale, exhale and optional hold seconds
interaction_types.guided_steps: Sequence of short timed instruction cards
interaction_types.text_prompt: One prompt with a free-text box (nothing is sent anywhere unless the user chooses)
interaction_types.checklist: Prompt plus a short list the user fills in
interaction_types.drawing_canvas: Canvas with an optional template (e.g. a mandala outline)
interaction_types.audio_player: Plays a calm or upbeat track the user picks; timer runs alongside
interaction_types.offscreen_card: Suggestion to do something away from the screen, with an optional timer and a 'done' button

meta.duration_note: duration_seconds is the recommended in-app length. short_version_seconds (<= 90 s) fits the current MVP format but is shorter than any tested dose for most activities; evidence_dose gives what studies actually used.

activities.title: Slow breathing
activities.subtitle: Breathe in for 4, out for 6
steps: Sit comfortably and let your shoulders drop.
Breathe in gently through your nose for 4 seconds.
Breathe out slowly for 6 seconds.
Keep it soft. No need to hold your breath.

activities.title: Tense and release
activities.subtitle: Let go of tension, one area at a time
steps: Make fists for 5 seconds, then let go for 10.
Lift your shoulders to your ears for 5 seconds, then drop them.
Scrunch your face for 5 seconds, then relax it.
Notice the difference between tense and relaxed.

activities.title: Calm music break
activities.subtitle: Five minutes of music you find soothing
steps: Pick a calm track you like.
Close your eyes or look somewhere soft.
Just listen until the timer ends.

activities.title: Physiological sigh
activities.subtitle: Double inhale, long slow exhale
steps: Breathe in through your nose.
Take a second, short sip of air on top.
Breathe out slowly and fully through your mouth.
Repeat at a comfortable pace.

activities.title: Talk to yourself like a friend
activities.subtitle: Use your own name to get some distance
steps: Think about what's stressing you.
Write two sentences about it using your name instead of 'I', e.g. 'Sam is worried because…'.
Add one sentence of advice you'd give a friend in Sam's place.

activities.title: Kind words to yourself
activities.subtitle: A short self-compassion pause
steps: Notice: 'This is a hard moment.'
Remember: 'Lots of people feel this way.'
Offer yourself one kind sentence, the way you would to a friend.

activities.title: Get it out of your head
activities.subtitle: List what's on your plate and the very next step
steps: List the things on your mind.
For one of them, write the very next small step and when you'll do it.
Let the list hold the rest for now.

activities.title: Picture a calm place
activities.subtitle: A short guided visualisation
steps: Close your eyes and picture a place where you feel at ease.
Notice what you can see, hear and feel there.
Stay with it for a few slow breaths.

activities.title: Something funny
activities.subtitle: A few minutes of comedy you enjoy
steps: Watch or listen to something that usually makes you laugh.
Come back and tap done when you're finished.

activities.title: Ten-minute walk
activities.subtitle: A brisk walk at your own pace
steps: Head outside or walk around indoors.
Pick a pace that feels brisk but comfortable.
Tap done when you're back.

steps: Write the worry in one line.
Pick a 15-minute 'worry time' later today.
Until then, when it comes back, remind yourself it's parked.

activities.title: Next small step
activities.subtitle: Turn one worry into a plan
steps: Write what you're worried might happen.
Write one small thing you can do about it, and when.
If there's nothing to do, note that too and let it rest.

activities.title: Calm music break
activities.subtitle: Five minutes of music you find soothing
steps: Pick a calm track you like.
Close your eyes or look somewhere soft.
Just listen until the timer ends.

activities.title: Get moving
activities.subtitle: 20 minutes of exercise you enjoy, at a comfortable pace
steps: Pick something you enjoy: a brisk walk, cycling, a home workout.
Keep the pace comfortable; you should still be able to talk.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
Tap done when you're back.

activities.title: Proper micro-break
activities.subtitle: Step away from the screen for a few minutes
steps: Look away from your screen.
Stretch, get a drink or look out of a window.
Come back when the timer ends.

activities.title: Stand up and move
activities.subtitle: A few minutes of light movement
steps: Stand up and roll your shoulders.
Walk around the room or march on the spot.
Reach up high, then shake out your arms.

activities.title: Ten-minute walk
activities.subtitle: A brisk walk for a lift in energy
steps: Head outside if you can.
Walk briskly but comfortably.
Tap done when you're back.

activities.title: Short power nap
activities.subtitle: Ten minutes, set an alarm
steps: Find somewhere you can lie down or rest your head.
Set an alarm for 10 minutes.
Not in the late afternoon or evening if it affects your sleep.

activities.title: Green view
activities.subtitle: Sit somewhere green, or look at trees through a window
steps: Find a green spot or a window with a view of trees or plants.
Let your eyes rest on it without your phone.
Tap done when you're ready.

activities.title: Get some daylight
activities.subtitle: Spend a few minutes in bright daylight
steps: Step outside or sit by a bright window during the day.
Stay for a few minutes.
Tap done when you're back.

activities.title: Take the stairs
activities.subtitle: Ten minutes of easy stair walking
steps: Walk up and down a flight of stairs at a gentle pace.
Hold the rail and stop if you feel unwell.
Tap done when you're finished.

activities.title: Dance it out
activities.subtitle: One upbeat song, move however you like
steps: Pick a song you like.
Move however feels good.
No one's watching.

activities.title: Kindness meditation
activities.subtitle: Send warm wishes to yourself and others
steps: Silently wish yourself: 'May I be well.'
Picture someone you care about and wish them the same.

activities.title: Three good photos
activities.subtitle: Photograph three things you like around you
steps: Look around for things that make you smile.
Take three photos.
Look back at them later today.

activities.title: Three good things
activities.subtitle: Note what's going well
steps: Write three things that went well or you're glad about.
For one of them, add why it happened.

activities.title: Colour a mandala
activities.subtitle: Keep the calm going with colour
steps: Pick colours you like.
Fill in the shapes at your own pace.

activities.title: Awe walk
activities.subtitle: A walk looking for things that amaze you
steps: Go for a short walk somewhere new or familiar.
Look for things that feel vast or surprising: sky, trees, buildings, details.
Tap done when you're back.

activities.title: Slow breathing
activities.subtitle: Stay in the calm
steps: Breathe in for 4 seconds.
Breathe out for 6 seconds.
Enjoy the stillness.

activities.title: Savour this moment
activities.subtitle: Stay with the good feeling a bit longer
steps: Notice what you're enjoying right now.
Replay the best part in your mind.

activities.title: Small kind act
activities.subtitle: Do one small thing for someone else
steps: Pick one small kind thing: a compliment, a thank-you, a helping hand.
Do it today.

activities.title: Share the good news

steps: Think of someone who'd be happy for you.
Send a message or call to tell them what went well.

activities.title: Best possible future

steps: Imagine a future where things have gone as well as they could.
Write about what it looks like.
Keep it realistic and specific.

activities.title: Thank-you note
activities.subtitle: Write to someone who helped you
steps: Think of someone you never properly thanked.
Write them a short note about what they did and why it mattered.

activities.title: Try something new

steps: Pick something small you've wanted to try: a new route, recipe or idea.
Give it a go for ten minutes.

activities.title: Dance it out

Move however feels good.

activities.title: Make something

steps: Make anything you like: a doodle, a short poem, a little design.
Play, don't judge.

existing_mvp_activity_notes.finding: No evidence for the 4-7-8 pattern itself was found in this research. The nearest evidence is for slow breathing at about 6 breaths a minute and for cyclic sighing (Balban et al. 2023; Fincham et al. 2023). The dataset's breathing guidance avoids long breath holds and fast breathing; no peer-reviewed source on breath-hold cautions was retrieved.
existing_mvp_activity_notes.suggestion: Keep the orb but offer a no-hold preset (in 4 s, out 6 s), or label 4-7-8 as a variation without its own evidence.

existing_mvp_activity_notes.finding: Not reviewed: the research did not cover pendulum or bilateral-tracking exercises.
existing_mvp_activity_notes.suggestion: Treat as unsupported until a source is found; do not add a citation for it.
